newsitem.title: UK: Morocco may begin buying wheat in mid-July - sources.
newsitem.headline: Morocco may begin buying wheat in mid-July - sources.

text.p: Moroccan private and public operators are expected to tap world markets for wheat in mid-July, purchasing an estimated 200,000 tonnes each month, possibly until May 1998, Moroccan grain industry sources said in London on Friday.

"Buyers should get in mid-July with the purchases averaging an estimated 200,000 tonnes of wheat each month," possibly until May, one source told a reporter at the London meeting of the International Grains Council.
Moroccan buyers are likely to favour U.S. wheat initially, because it already available in the market and cheaper than other origins, the sources said.
But the European Union and eastern European countries that expect significantly higher crops this year will also get a share of the market.
Morocco which has been hit by drought this year is expected to harvest 2.0 million tonnes of wheat in 1997/98 against 5.9 million in 1996/97, the latest projections from the IGC suggest.
